name: SPOTIO
description: SPOTIO is a field-sales engagement platform for managing leads, territories, routes, rep activity, appointments, pipelines, communications, integrations, analytics, and mobile sales execution. Teams use it to capture location-verified field activity and synchronize structured sales data with CRM and ERP systems.
agentUseSummary: Add a customer-owned dedicated SPOTIO Admin API Client ID and Secret plus one exact 24-character hexadecimal data-object ID. Agents may read only that bound object's privacy-redacted type, stage, source, creation/update times, stage-update time, and bounded visit/call counts; Relay excludes names, phones, emails, address/GPS, owners, territories, fields, notes, activities, communication, searches, exports, writes, webhooks, raw APIs, and provider MCP surfaces.

blocked.label: Change data objects
blocked.description: Creating, patching, moving, deleting, restoring, assigning, or changing data objects, fields, stages, pins, activities, appointments, documents, and related records is outside V1.

blocked.label: Access people, location, or private content
blocked.description: Names, phones, emails, addresses, GPS coordinates, place IDs, owners, collaborators, territories, custom fields, notes, attachments, and raw records are never returned.

blocked.label: Communicate with prospects
blocked.description: Calls, email, text, templates, campaigns, autoplays, multichannel communication, signatures, notifications, and prospect outreach are outside V1.

blocked.label: Access account or administration
blocked.description: Users, teams, business cards, workflow definitions, layouts, SSO, connectors, API keys, bearer tokens, webhooks, reports, calendars, routes, trips, tracking, billing, and administration are outside V1.

blocked.label: Call raw or bulk surfaces
blocked.description: Raw REST, arbitrary endpoints, searches, filters, pagination, polling, exports, imports, bulk jobs, downloads, crawling, and provider MCP surfaces are outside V1.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The bounded private data-object summary read requires matching approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The selected summary read runs without Relay approval while exact object binding, token exchange, fixed endpoint, audit, redaction, and response bounds remain enforced; people, location, content, communication, writes, administration, and bulk work stay blocked.

providerSetup.blocker: No customer-owned paid SPOTIO workspace, dedicated Admin-generated API Client ID and one-time Secret, exact preconfigured data-object ID, or live API acceptance evidence is available in this workspace.
providerSetup.nextAction: In the provider-console task use the intended paid SPOTIO workspace and a durable least-privileged Admin-managed integration user to create dedicated API keys under Settings > Integrations > API Access, record one exact existing 24-character data-object ID, store all three values through Relay, then validate token exchange, the fixed bound GET, field redaction, approval/denial, token renewal, rate-limit handling, key rotation, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial without changing records or communicating with prospects.

evidence.supports: Official quickstart documents the https://api.spotio2.com base URL, Client ID and Secret exchange at POST /api/users/apitoken, bearer authentication, and the REST reference.

Official authentication guidance requires Admin-created API keys from Settings > Integrations > API Access, says keys inherit the creating user's role and privileges, instructs secure storage, and documents 30-day bearer tokens and 401 expiry behavior.

Official reference documents fixed GET /api/DataObjects/{dataObjectId} and shows that a record can contain names, owners, address and GPS data, territories, custom fields, phone and email values, collaborators, visit/call state, and timestamps; Relay returns only the bound ID and a narrow metadata subset.

Official guide describes configurable sales records, workflow fields and stages, searches, creation and patching, and examples containing names, addresses, coordinates, owners, phone and email data; Relay blocks all search and mutation surfaces.

Official webhook guidance documents lead, activity, and appointment events with HMAC signatures and payloads containing identity, contact, address, and location data; V1 does not register or receive webhooks.

Official terms require account security, internal authorized-user use, customer rights and consent for licensed content, and consent before email, call, or text communication with prospects; Relay blocks communication and private-surface automation.
Official security material describes SOC 2 Type II controls, encryption, role-based access, audit logs, Azure hosting, and the sensitivity of GPS-verified field activity.
